newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM vows to help find Kashmir hostages.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM vows to help find Kashmir hostages.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Wednesday pledged to do everything possible to help find four Western hostages held in the Indian-ruled part of the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.
Sharif gave the assurance at a meeting in Islamabad with relatives of the two British hostages, his spokesman said.

He quoted the prime minister as telling the group that he was committed to helping bring the kidnap drama to an early end and felt "duty-bound to do everything possible to ascertain the whereabouts of the hostages".
Earlier, the group told a news conference they wanted more than mere appeals from everybody of any influence to help find their loved ones.

Britons Paul Wells and Keith Mangan were abducted by the shadowy Al-Faran guerrilla group while trekking in Indian Kashmir in July 1995. German Dirk Hasert, Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe and Americans Donald Hutchings and John Childs were also captured.
Childs escaped and Ostroe was beheaded. There has been no trace of the other four for several months, raising doubts over whether they are still alive.

India has linked a pro-Pakistan militant group, Harkat-ul-Ansar, to the kidnapping. But the group denies any involvement in the kidnapping and any links with Al-Faran and has accused the Indian authorities of masterminding the kidnapping to defame a Moslem revolt against India in the region.
Harkat issued its own appeal earlier this month for the hostages' release.

"Everybody has made appeals but these appeals have fallen on deaf ears," Julie Mangan, wife of British hostage Keith Mangan, told the Islamabad news conference. "This time we want more than appeals. We want an active appeal," she said.
Her group has already visited India and both Indian- and Pakistan-ruled parts of Kashmir and met officials and Kashmiri group leaders.

"Our message has been the same in each location, which is that we simply want the truth," said Bob Wells, father of hostage Paul Wells. "We need to know the fate and whereabouts of our loved ones," he added.
"We appeal to all the people to please come forward, if they have some information about the place, or the health of the hostages," Wells said.

Several Moslem militant groups are fighting Indian rule over two-thirds of Kashmir. Pakistan controls the remaining third of the region, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since winning independence from Britain in 1947.
